question: Should the sponsor fund delivery discovery, hold the proposal, or reject it?

next_action.description: Review the proposal and select one of the recorded options.

options.name: Proceed to delivery discovery
benefits: Tests process and architecture assumptions before implementation.
costs: Requires a separately funded discovery engagement.
risks: Discovery may falsify assumptions in the preliminary proposal.

options.name: Hold
benefits: Preserves the proposal while the sponsor resolves timing or budget.
costs: Evidence and estimates may become stale.
risks: The business problem may continue without mitigation.

options.name: Reject
benefits: Avoids spending on an engagement the sponsor does not value.
costs: Ends this proposed path to the desired business outcome.
risks: The underlying scheduling problem remains unresolved.

recommendation.rationale: The proposal is complete enough to justify bounded discovery but not to authorize implementation.
assumptions: The sponsor still values reducing scheduling delays.
tradeoffs: Discovery adds cost now in exchange for reducing implementation risk later.

assumptions: A bounded delivery-discovery phase is commercially acceptable.
